customer_jordan: Hey team — We've started seeing intermittent JSON parse failures in production after turning on prefix caching + request batching on the hosted API. Happens ~1/200 requests.

customer_jordan: Example symptom: two separate responses appear merged into a single JSON payload (fields from request A get concatenated into request B) and the client can't parse it. Not sure if this is streaming-related.

support_amy: Sorry you're hitting this — can you share a raw response body and a couple of request IDs? Also: are you using json_mode=true or a post-processing schema check? streaming=yes/no?

customer_jordan: Providing two request ids: req_5a1c2f and req_5a1c31. Raw payloads attached below (pasted):

customer_jordan: ```
-- raw response for req_5a1c2f --
{"orderId":"ord_903","items":[{"sku":"A1","qty":1}],"total":120}
-- raw response for req_5a1c31 (expected) --
{"orderId":"ord_904","items":[{"sku":"B2","qty":2}],"total":240}
-- actual observed merged response returned to client --
{"orderId":"ord_903","items":[{"sku":"A1","qty":1}]{"sku":"B2","qty":2}],"total":120240}
```

support_amy: Thanks. That merged example is super helpful. A few clarification q's:
- Are you sending multiple prompts in a single batch call (array inputs) or relying on server-side batching?
- Which model variant / runtime flags? (ex: redwood/open-llm-13b-instruct, quantized=int8, streaming=true)
- Any custom post-processing that strips whitespace or concatenates streams?

customer_jordan: We're using server-side automatic batching (we send single prompt per request). Model: redwood/open-llm-13b-instruct, quantized=int8, streaming=true, json_mode=true. We also enabled prefix_cache on the deployment to speed up repeated system prompts. Batch size autoscale peaks at 8-16. No custom stream concat logic on our side.

eng_runtime_rory: Looping in runtime — this looks like a race where response fragments from different requests are being interleaved when batching + streaming + prefix cache are enabled. Hypothesis: the assembler that composes tokens per-request may not be isolating cached prefix completions from concurrent live generations, leading to missing separators (comma) or duplicated bracket closure.

eng_runtime_rory: Quick repro ask: can you run the following locally against the hosted endpoint to confirm? It simulates high concurrency with streaming + json_mode.

eng_runtime_rory: ```bash
seq 1 40 | xargs -n1 -P8 -I{} curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/open-llm-13b-instruct","stream":true,"json_mode":true,"input":"{\"order\": \"{\"id\": \"IDX{}\"}\"}"}'
```

devex_mark: One quick troubleshooting step: try setting RW_DISABLE_PREFIX_CACHE=true in your request headers (we can also flip it for your deployment) to see if the issue stops. If it does, prefix cache interaction with the streaming assembler is likely the culprit.

customer_jordan: Will try RW_DISABLE_PREFIX_CACHE=true now. Meanwhile, can you explain why batcher would mix tokens across requests? We thought each request had its own output buffer.

eng_runtime_rory: Short version: the batcher pools token generation calls to the GPU and then demultiplexes token streams back to request buffers. There's a small code path where cached prefix completions are appended to the global output stream without being attached to the per-request demux key, especially when cache hits occur right as a pooled live generation flushes. That can produce two fragments back-to-back with no delimiter.

eng_runtime_rory: Action items from runtime side:
- We'll add extra request_id tagging inside the streaming frames and ensure cached prefix emissions are wrapped with start/end markers.
- I opened internal ticket ENG-REPRO-1234 and assigned it to eng-runtime.

deploy-bot: Deployment planned: runtime/patch/stream-demux-tagging to staged cluster tomorrow 03:00 UTC (canary 10%).

support_amy: For immediate mitigation we can:
- Disable prefix_cache for your account (temporary)
- Force stream=false (non-streaming) which will assemble whole response server-side per-request
- If you can accept added latency, set batching.max_batch_size=1 for your route to avoid pooling.

customer_jordan: Disabling prefix cache fixed it in a small smoke test. Thanks.

eng_ml_sunita: Also recommendation for customers: enable a short JSON schema validation on SDK side to fail fast and surface exactly where the parse error happened. We'll add an automated alert rule to detect if parse_failure_rate > 0.1% for a route.

support_amy: We'll keep this thread updated. Jordan, we'll coordinate a scheduled canary of the runtime patch and let you know before we enable prefix cache again. Sorry for the disruption — thanks for quick repro.

customer_jordan: Appreciate it. Please keep me posted on ENG-REPRO-1234 and the canary results. :thanks:
